difficulty_reason: In the situation of the taut descent statements of the chapter, the lemma asserts that if the target ring is weakly pre-admissible then so is the source (statement lines 1820-1825). The proof fixes a weak ideal of definition of the target and an open ideal of the source whose extension lies inside it, and reduces the assertion to showing that every element of that open ideal is topologically nilpotent (proof lines 1827-1830). For an arbitrary open ideal of the source, it lets the closure of its extension be the corresponding ideal of the target; faithfulness of flatness of the map between the quotients makes that map injective, so it suffices to see that a power of the image of the element lies in that closure, which holds because the image lies in a weak ideal of definition of the target and the closure is open (proof lines 1830-1836). The claim is H2: the reduction to a nilpotence statement is followed by an argument that descends the required containment along a faithfully flat map, both steps displayed.
